_comment: Connector-specific edits to GENERATED/authored files that a cli-printing-press reprint must NOT clobber. check_handfixes.py asserts every marker below is still present (and banned anti-patterns absent) and fails CI if a reprint dropped one. Provenance: live-verification report from Abhi Saini (Bearium Networks) in the Compounding Teams Community Discussion, 2026-08-13 (badge flip PR #199).

handfixes.summary: parseTenantArray unwraps a {"Results": [...]} envelope before falling back to the lone-tenant path, so --all-tenants fan-out enumerates the fleet
handfixes.why: Current CIPP returns /ListTenants as {"Results":[...]}; the novel cross-tenant code only handled a bare array and fell back to 'treat the whole payload as one tenant object'. That object resolves no defaultDomainName, gets dropped, and every --all-tenants fan-out reports ZERO tenants against a healthy CIPP with a 6.6 KB response on the wire. The rest of the tree already knew the key - promoted_list-tenants.go writes the store from "Results" and sync.go's pageItemKeys lists results/Results - only the novel path missed it. cipp_tenants.go is a NOVEL (non-generated) file, so this survives a reprint as a carried novel; the assert guards against a novel-rewrite dropping it.

handfixes.summary: The client re-mints the OAuth2 client-credentials access token when it nears expiry, and `auth login` persists the tenant_id/authority/scope that a re-mint needs
handfixes.why: As generated, `auth login` cached an access token plus a token_expiry that NOTHING ever read: config.AuthHeader() returned 'Bearer '+access_token forever and client.go retried only 429/5xx, never 401. Azure AD client-credentials tokens live about 60 to 90 minutes, so a cipp install stopped working roughly an hour after login and every request 401'd until a human re-ran `auth login`. The long-lived MCP server re-reads config.toml per tool call, so it kept serving the dead token indefinitely. The generated `auth login` also accepted --tenant-id and DISCARDED it, leaving no Azure AD token endpoint to refresh against; tenant_id, authority and scope are now persisted, and a config that predates them fails with an actionable error naming the exact command rather than silently reproducing the 401. Three constraints are load-bearing and easy for a reprint or a well-meaning refactor to undo: (1) the re-mint predicate must NOT be the sibling connectors' 'empty access_token means mint', because cipp's documented static CIPP_API_KEY mode has an empty access_token permanently and would mint on every request behind a package-level mutex, serializing the entire fan-out; (2) the mint must ride c.HTTPClient, not http.DefaultClient, or it escapes the test harness, --dry-run and verify mode; (3) the save must be best-effort, unlike the nine sibling connectors that return a wrapped error and throw away a valid token on a read-only home dir. Covered by internal/client/token_refresh_test.go, internal/config/oauth_context_test.go and internal/cli/auth_token_context_test.go. An adversarial review then found the ledger itself was presence-only: every assert pinned a string INSIDE a helper, so a reprint that regenerated authHeader() would drop the four-line CALL SITE while every asserted string survived as dead code - green CI, fix gone. The call site is now asserted verbatim.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: the generated client.go emits a stub authHeader with no expiry gate even when the connector's auth flow is client_credentials, and the generated config.Config carries no tenant/authority/scope/token_url fields for an Azure AD grant. Six connectors in this repo mint a token and never refresh it: cipp, blumira, microsoft-graph, kaseya-bms, datto-rmm, quickbooks. blumira and microsoft-graph carry a byte-identical stub and the same missing-tenant gap, so this fix ports directly to them.

handfixes.summary: The client-credentials token exchange refuses cross-origin redirects, degrades to the still-valid cached token when a re-mint fails, clamps its refresh skew to half the granted lifetime, and masks client_secret in the token endpoint's error body
handfixes.why: Four defects an adversarial review found in the re-mint above, all of them regressions a reprint or a well-meaning refactor would reintroduce. (1) SECURITY: the mint set `cp.CheckRedirect = nil` to dodge a ccMu re-entrancy deadlock. Clearing CheckRedirect does not disable redirects - it restores Go's DEFAULT policy, which follows up to 10 hops and REPLAYS THE POST BODY on 307/308. That body is the client-credentials form carrying client_secret, so the single most secret-bearing request in the CLI was the only one that opted out of the threat model client.New()'s own CheckRedirect states ('a cross-domain 3xx must not receive the auth credential'), and the CLI then accepted and cached whatever access_token the redirect target returned. `auth login` had the identical hole via http.DefaultClient. Both now install TokenExchangeRedirectPolicy, which is a plain function over its arguments: it closes over no *Client and no package state, so a same-origin comparison cannot re-enter ccMu the way the authHeader-calling policy did. Do NOT 'simplify' it back to nil, and do NOT make it a *Client method that reads c.Config. (2) AVAILABILITY: a failed mint returned its error straight to authHeader, so during the 5-minute safety skew - about 8% of every token lifetime - any transient token-endpoint failure (AAD 5xx, DNS, proxy blip) converted a working CLI into a broken one while the cached token was still perfectly valid. mintFailureWithCachedToken now makes the same judgement remintUnavailable already made for the missing-tenant_id case: warn and proceed while the token is genuinely alive, fail hard only once it is actually spent. A 30-second cooldown keeps a fan-out from re-attempting a known-down endpoint on every request while HOLDING ccMu for up to tokenRequestTimeout apiece. (3) MINT STORM: the predicate compared the remaining lifetime against a fixed 5-minute skew, so a token endpoint granting anything shorter than 10 minutes put every freshly minted token inside the skew the instant it arrived - re-minting on every request and serializing the whole fan-out behind the package-level mutex. effectiveTokenSkew clamps to half the granted lifetime, which needs the new non-secret config field token_lifetime to survive to disk. (4) SECRET IN ERROR: the mint's HTTP-error path used cliutil.SanitizeErrorBody, which only knows generic token shapes and has never seen cfg.ClientSecret, because the real masker c.maskCredentialText takes ccMu and the mint already holds it. maskCredentialTextLocked is the lock-free variant; it runs BEFORE SanitizeErrorBody because that helper truncates at 200 bytes and a secret straddling the boundary would no longer match its own needle. Covered by internal/client/token_hardening_test.go, internal/cli/auth_login_redirect_test.go and internal/config/token_lifetime_test.go, each proved in both directions.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: every generated client_credentials mint in this repo has the same three holes. The press should emit a same-origin CheckRedirect on any token exchange (never a nil one), should degrade a failed re-mint to a still-valid cached token, and should record the granted expires_in so the refresh skew can be clamped. Six connectors mint a token this way: cipp, blumira, microsoft-graph, kaseya-bms, datto-rmm, quickbooks.

handfixes.summary: doctor probes a real GET endpoint with the real credential and refuses to dial a placeholder base_url, instead of calling any HTTP response 'reachable' and never checking the credential
handfixes.why: `doctor` is the command every SKILL, guide and docs page tells an operator to run to confirm the connector works, and it could not tell a working install from a broken one. It called any HTTP response to `GET /` "reachable" and rendered it green, so a base_url aimed at the vendor's web UI (where every API path 404s) and a token rejected with 401 on every call both produced an all-green report. On this connector family it also never probed the credential at all: it printed "present, not verified" and left the operator to guess. The mirror defect: a connector whose shipped base_url default is a placeholder dialled the placeholder host, and the DNS failure rendered as "FAIL API: unreachable" - telling a correctly-credentialled operator they were broken without naming the one variable that would fix it. Several placeholder hosts resolve through live wildcard DNS and answer real HTTP, so dialling one produced a confident green verdict against a stranger's server. Measured and gated by tools/maintainer/check_doctor_truth.py. See issue #282.

asserts.contains: report["credentials"] = "ERROR not verified: no credential is configured, so nothing was probed."
report["api"] = "not configured (base_url is a placeholder); set " + doctorBaseURLEnv + " to your own instance URL"

handfixes.summary: every operator credential this connector reads is declared on all three install channels: manifest.json (.mcpb), server.json (MCP Registry) and mcp-install.md (manual install)
handfixes.why: Issue #282 ('three live-verified connectors prompt for the wrong credentials'). A connector is installed through THREE independent channels that each carry their own copy of the credential list: manifest.json server.mcp_config.env (what the .mcpb bundle hands Claude Desktop, which has no shell profile, no config.toml and no export - so an undeclared variable is a variable nobody is ever asked for), server.json environmentVariables (the MCP Registry publish channel), and mcp-install.md's copy-paste JSON blocks plus its remote launch line (the manual path, which never touches the bundle at all). The fleet-wide audit found 60 of 65 connectors under-declaring 122 operator-facing variables in the manifest, 61 of 65 mcp-install.md pages omitting 125, and hudu's server.json missing the base URL its manifest marks required. For cipp the manifest gained: CIPP_BASE_URL. server.json gained: CIPP_BASE_URL. mcp-install.md's env blocks gained: CIPP_BASE_URL. manifest.json, server.json and mcp-install.md are ALL regenerated by /msp-skills-publish on an UPDATE or re-onboard, so without this ledger a regeneration silently drops every declaration and CI stays green (check_env_schema.py is wired --warn). The asserts below name the specific credentials, not a count, so dropping one and adding another cannot cancel out.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should emit server.mcp_config.env, the matching user_config prompts, server.json environmentVariables and mcp-install.md's env blocks from ONE declaration of the connector's operator-facing environment, so the three channels cannot be generated out of step. Until then check_env_schema.py compares all three and this ledger pins them.

handfixes.summary: CIPP_NO_CONFIG_WRITE makes every credential write a no-op (token cache included) while leaving the `auth logout` erase working, and the MCP server honours it too (issue #270)
handfixes.why: Issue #270, raised by @Xenith-B off the back of #266. #266 stopped env-supplied client credentials reaching disk; the MINTED access token still landed in ~/.config/<tool>-cli/config.toml in cleartext and there was no supported way to turn that off. Their workaround was `--config NUL`, which is OS-specific, undocumented, makes doctor report a false 'not configured', and - the part that matters most - does not cover the MCP servers at all, because internal/mcp resolved its own hardcoded config path and ignored --config. Three deliberate boundaries make this switch honest rather than merely quiet. (1) ClearTokens keeps calling save() directly: it is the ERASE path, and routing it through the guard would make `auth logout` silently inert, which is a worse defect than the one being fixed. (2) `auth login` and `auth set-token` REFUSE and name the variable rather than reporting a save that did not happen - a false success is the same defect class as a doctor that says credentials are fine without checking. (3) newMCPClient now resolves through config.Load(""), the resolver the CLI uses, so the MCP server honours both CIPP_CONFIG and this switch; that is the half the issue says is uncovered today. The variable is declared on all three install channels because for a Claude Desktop install the manifest prompt is the ONLY channel that can set an environment variable. Class C, new documented surface. GENERATOR-class: a reprint drops the switch entirely and silently restores the plaintext token cache.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should emit <PREFIX>_NO_CONFIG_WRITE (or an equivalent) as part of the standard config surface, with the same three boundaries: the erase path exempt, explicit save commands failing loudly rather than no-oping, and the MCP server resolving its config through config.Load("") instead of a hardcoded home-relative path. The hardcoded path in internal/mcp/tools.go is a generator defect in its own right - it makes --config and <PREFIX>_CONFIG inert for every MCP install on every connector.

asserts.contains: | `auth login` / `auth set-token` | Refuse, naming the variable, instead of reporting a save that did not happen. |

handfixes.summary: MCP discovery exposes executor-facing request schemas and indexes input names and known enum values
handfixes.why: Issue #351: endpoint summaries omitted required request inputs. Keep canonical JSON body case and nesting, path/header/query routing, and exact short request search terms. Contracts are derived from the shipped CLI source, and the existing CLI commands and auth remain intact. Upstream request metadata fix #4890 was not merged when this surgical repair was made.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Replace this downstream contract extraction only when a released Printing Press generates equally complete executor-facing schemas and preserves every existing hand-fix.

handfixes.summary: add-intune-reusable-setting-template takes the body's json field as --json-field instead of a local --json, so --json is the JSON-output switch on every command; the body still carries its json field
handfixes.why: A command-local flag that takes a value, registered under the name of a persistent root switch, replaces that switch on its command: Cobra keeps the command's own flag. Every SKILL, guide and MCP recipe tells an agent to add --json for JSON output, so on this command a bare --json stopped with 'flag needs an argument', and --json followed by another flag swallowed that flag as its value (halopsa `tickets list --agent --dry-run` sent the live request: the --dry-run became the agent filter). The press does not reserve the root flag names when it names spec parameters (internal/generator/flag_collision.go reserves only its own --all/--wait/--stdin), so a reprint re-emits the shadow. tools/maintainer/check_command_tree.py now fails any value-taking local flag over a persistent switch.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: reserve the root persistent flag names (agent, json, dry-run, quiet, ...) in reservedFlagNamesForEndpoint so a spec parameter of the same name gets a distinct public flag; until then, keep the rename here.

handfixes.summary: One decoded output funnel for every server text the client shows: maskCredentialText (every API error, transport error, displayed URL and --dry-run parameter goes through it) still masks each held credential as written and URL-escaped, then withholds the WHOLE text if any held value survives in any view reachable by undoing control/format characters, JSON and JavaScript escapes, percent escapes at any depth, HTML entities, markup tags, and base64/base64url/hex runs at every alignment (cliutil.FunnelWithhold, shared byte-identical across the fleet). The held set is every value the masks cover plus the part after a scheme word and both halves of a base64 id:secret pair (Basic auth, composed keys). Surfaces funnelled here: the API error body (checked whole before the 4096-byte display cut, then again as shown). The `auth login` token request (internal/cli/auth_login.go cippClientCredentialsToken) funnels its error body with the client secret it sent. Round 3 (owner-approved structural pass): the decoder searches every view breadth-first over one fixed set of steps (control-character drop, JSON and JavaScript escapes, the identity escape as its own step, percent, HTML entities, tag strip, base64 at four alignments, hex at two), matches every view, the original included, before any filter, keeps every view a step makes (a literal backslash survives), deduplicates, and is capped by total work (512 times the input plus 4 MiB; text over 1 MiB or past the cap is withheld). Every value a funnel call is given is held process-wide (cliutil.FunnelHold), and the client holds its credentials when built and its resolved auth header on every request. Two error-only backstops withhold any held value: every command error before Cobra prints it plus every JSON/agent error envelope (internal/cli/secret_funnel_cli.go), and every MCP error result and handler error through the outermost tool middleware (cmd/<mcp>/secret_funnel_mcp.go). Success output is never funnelled. The `auth login` token function funnels the complete body (after its own in-place mask) once, before the Azure AD JSON branch formats error and error_description, closing the round-2 input; TestAuthLogin_AADErrorBranchWithholdsEncodedSecret pins it.
handfixes.why: class_harness.py secret-echo (Step 3.1, PR #436) drives the built CLI and MCP server against a fake server that reflects each configured credential in every encoding; on origin/main this connector printed the credential HTML-entity-encoded, JSON-escaped, double URL-encoded or base64 (the generated masks cover only the raw, QueryEscape and PathEscape forms; press issue #5145). Matching encoded needles one at a time never converged (saas-alerts and cisco-meraki review loops), so the fix is a decode-then-check backstop that withholds the whole text and fails closed (text over 4 MiB, a decoding chain that does not settle in 32 rounds, or work past the budget is withheld). Classification is kept: the plain withheld notice avoids every word the auth-error classifiers match, and a withheld text that itself read as an auth failure gets a notice that says so (an HTTP 400 'invalid token' answer echoing the token keeps its auth exit code). Codex round 1 (2026-10-23) added that, the fail-closed depth bound (a text-like layer left at depth 8 withholds), the JavaScript escapes \v, \0 and the identity escape, a bounded \u{ search, and the token-endpoint error bodies outside the client. Known limits: values under 8 characters are only masked as written; case-changed, split-and-interleaved or otherwise transformed (compressed, encrypted) echoes are not reconstructed. A reprint that drops these edits fails class_harness.py secret-echo in CI and these asserts.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: cli-printing-press issue #5145 (encoded credential echo). The generated maskCredentialText should end in a decode-then-check backstop over every held credential, and the error-body and token-endpoint paths should check the whole body before the display cut.

handfixes.summary: The MCP context tool compacts its endpoint catalog when the payload would exceed bound.MaxBytes.
handfixes.why: About 560 endpoints make the resources catalog larger than bound.MaxBytes, and bound.JSON then falls back to a preview envelope that drops tool_count, auth and every other top-level field; the generated TestMCPContextMatchesRegisteredToolSurface fails on a raw 4.34.0 render. A reprint re-emits the uncompacted catalog.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: the context tool should size its catalog to bound.MaxBytes for large surfaces.

handfixes.summary: detectPartialFailure delegates to the CIPP Results-envelope parser first, so a write CIPP answers with HTTP 200 and a failure string is detected (bulk and the non-promoted write commands exit non-zero; the promoted typed commands still exit 0, see the docs).
handfixes.why: CIPP hardcodes HTTP 200 on several write entrypoints and reports failures as prose inside a Results array. The generated detector only matches Google Ads' partialFailureError object, so a failed write exited 0. cipp_results.go is hand-written; the delegation in generated helpers.go is what a reprint drops.

handfixes.summary: auth login performs the CIPP API client's OAuth2 client-credentials exchange (hand-written auth_login.go, wired into the generated auth command).
handfixes.why: The spec declares only bearer auth, so the press emits no login command; without this wiring an operator has no way to mint a token from the CIPP API client CIPP issues.

handfixes.summary: A non-2xx token-endpoint body is redacted structurally (token members removed, escaped JSON included) before it is shown, and a negative expires_in is refused.
handfixes.why: An authority answering 4xx with a token in the body would print that token in the error. Codex rounds 1 to 3 on the reprint found a \u-escaped token value slipping past a regex-only redaction; JSON bodies are now parsed, redacted and re-serialized. A negative expires_in would stamp an expiry in the past and re-mint on every request. Codex round 1 on the publish branch: a token member whose NAME is escaped (access\u005ftoken inside a prefixed error_description) slipped past both; the text is now decoded layer by layer and withheld whole if a token member survives.

handfixes.summary: fanout --save replaces a tenant's stored rows in one transaction, and only from a well-formed list: a JSON array, or an envelope whose Results is an array, whose every element is an object carrying the endpoint's identity key (an id-class field: id, _id, id_, uuid, guid, Identity, RowKey; or, from the CIPP-API source, UPN/PrimarySmtpAddress for /ListMailboxForwarding, displayName for /ListStandards, GroupId for /ListGDAPRoles, skuId for /ListLicenses). JSON null, an empty body, a duplicate key, a lone object, a string or any other shape is shown and not stored, the tenant is reported as an error and not checkpointed, and the stored rows stay. A response with any failure signal is refused before that (tenant-list-message-is-not-a-fleet).
handfixes.why: Saving by upsert kept rows CIPP no longer returns, an envelope was stored as one row, and a Results array mixing rows with a failure string was saved as the complete set, deleting rows it omitted (Codex round 3 on the reprint; TestFanoutPartialResultWithMessageKeepsRows). Batch 1b Codex round 1: a lone {"id":"error-1","error":"HTTP 403"} was saved as the whole user list and deleted u1 and u2. Batch 1b Codex round 2: a bare JSON null decoded as an empty list and deleted u1 and u2.

handfixes.summary: fanout accepts only List*/Get* read endpoints, so it can never drive an action endpoint across every tenant.
handfixes.why: fanout is an MCP tool. Before the guard an MCP call could fan /ExecSendOrgMessage or /RemoveStandard across every tenant with no confirmation step.

handfixes.summary: bulk (CSV-driven writes) is hidden from the MCP server and its --from file flag is never an MCP argument.
handfixes.why: bulk reads a host file and executes writes across tenants. Press 4.34.0's blocked MCP input set does not include "from", which the retired mcp-filesystem-destination-gate used to cover.

handfixes.summary: Rows fanout saves are keyed on (id, tenant), so two tenants sharing an id (license SKUs) no longer overwrite each other.
handfixes.why: CIPP returns the same id in many tenants (SKU ids, policy template ids); keying the store on id alone kept only the last tenant's row.

handfixes.summary: With CIPP_NO_LOCAL_DATA=1, fanout --save and --resume refuse before anything is written; a live fanout without them still runs.
handfixes.why: Press 4.34.0's no-local-data switch blocks the generated sync and workflow archive commands, but cipp fills its store with the hand-written fanout --save, which the switch did not reach: an operator who chose no local copy still got every tenant's rows on disk.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: let a novel command declare itself a local-data writer so applyLocalDataEnv refuses it with the generated ones.

handfixes.summary: posture --dimension mfa reads the rows fanout saved from /ListMFAUsers, which carry the MFA registration fields.
handfixes.why: Earlier builds read /ListUsers, which carries no MFA fields, so every user could count as missing MFA. Reported by CIPP's author on 2026-10-22.

handfixes.summary: cipp_execute returns an error result when a state-changing call comes back HTTP 200 with a failure inside CIPP's Results.
handfixes.why: CIPP answers several writes (EditUser, ExecOffboardUser, AddScheduledItem) with HTTP 200 and the failure as text in Results. The generated executor returned it as a successful tool result, so an agent reported a failed offboard as done (Codex round 1 on the publish branch).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: let a connector register a response-body failure detector the executor applies to write results.

handfixes.summary: export and tail refuse a resource whose path is not a CIPP read (List*/Get*), so neither can GET a state-changing action endpoint.
handfixes.why: CIPP names 43 state-changing endpoints as GET actions (ExecExtensionClearHIBPKey, ExecRunBackup, RemoveStandard). The generated export command is an MCP tool and accepted them as resources, so an MCP call ran one with no preview or confirm (Codex round 1 on the publish branch); tail would poll one repeatedly.

handfixes.summary: The tenant list, the GDAP relationship list and every fanout response go through ONE document walker (cippScan, shared with write results). It walks the whole response, envelope and every element at any depth, and any failure signal anywhere refuses the whole response: failure wording (word boundary) in a string under a status-like key (lowercased name contains state, status, result, message, msg, text, detail, reason or fail) or in a bare message string, a populated key whose lowercased name contains error, exception or fault, a key named like success, succeeded or ok (ok as a whole word: isOk, OK, not outlook or token) holding false or "false", and a state/status-like key holding a failure state. Stored rows stay. Status-like ancestry: any value at any depth under a status-like key is checked ({"status":{"code":"error"}}), except the document's own row container (a top-level array, or the Results/data/value/items array of a top-level envelope). Every body is decoded strictly: a duplicate object key at any depth (compared case-insensitively) refuses the list. The one exemption applies only when validating the tenant LIST, never to write results or any other response: each tenant row's own LastGraphError, LastGraphTokenError and GraphErrorCount (that tenant's Graph token state). The tenant and GDAP lists also require every element to be an object carrying the identity key (defaultDomainName, id). A row whose own name or description holds a failure word (a user named "Error Reporting", a group named "Denied Access") is still a row. Write results still read failure wording in any string (cipp-results-failure-vocabulary). Trade-off (documented): a list whose rows report their own failed status is refused; run fanout with --json to see what CIPP returned.
handfixes.why: CIPP appends a failure string to a partial list. tenantEnvelopeArray kept the objects and dropped the string, so fanout --all-tenants ran on part of the fleet and saved it as the tenant list, and gdap expiring could report covered tenants as uncovered (Codex round 1 on the publish branch). Codex round 3: a structured failure entry ({"state":"error","resultText":"Failed to retrieve remaining tenants"}) passed as a row and was then dropped for having no domain, so fanout ran on part of the fleet. Fresh Codex round 1: a failure object carrying an id passed as a row (fanout --save deleted p2), and an envelope-level error beside a partial Results list was discarded (the stored tenant list lost b.example). Fresh Codex round 2: the field list omitted status, text, msg, detail and details, so {"id":"error-1","status":"error"} passed and an envelope "status":"error" was ignored. Fresh Codex round 3: an element {"id":"error-1","error":"HTTP 403"} and an envelope "error":"HTTP 403" passed because "HTTP 403" carries no failure word; the populated error field is now the signal. CIPP's own tenant records carry LastGraphError (Get-Tenants.ps1, Get-GraphToken.ps1), so without the tenant-record exemption one tenant with a failed Graph token would refuse the whole fleet. Batch 1b Codex round 1: each check looked at part of the response, so an element {"id":"partial","success":false} passed and fanout --save deleted u2. Orchestrator decision after batch 1b round 1: failure wording anywhere refused healthy lists (a user named "Error Reporting"), and none of Codex's inputs needed it; lists read wording only under status-like keys, every structural signal stays. Batch 1b Codex round 2: the tenant-record exemption also hid a write failure in a tenant-shaped write answer; a failure nested under "status" beside a partial list was ignored; a duplicate key let the last value win.

handfixes.summary: A failed token request prints no vendor prose: only an OAuth error code from a fixed enum (RFC 6749 plus Azure AD's interaction_required, temporarily_unavailable, server_error) and the AADSTS error numbers found in error_description; everything else is withheld. Every error built from a token-endpoint answer, 2xx or not, including JSON decode and type errors, is described by kind only ("token response could not be decoded", "token response contained no access_token") plus that allowlisted code and the AADSTS numbers when the body is an Azure AD error (TokenResponseError); never body text and never a Go decoder message, which quotes the input. Both auth login and the client re-mint.

handfixes.summary: A CIPP write result is tri-state, decided by the one document walker (cippScan, shared with list validation) over the WHOLE response document, the envelope beside Results as much as Results itself: failure wording in any string value (word boundary, plus camelCase failure codes), a populated key whose lowercased name contains error, exception or fault (non-empty string, non-zero number, object or non-empty array), a key named like success, succeeded or ok holding false or "false", and a state/status-like key holding a failure state. Any failure signal plus any success signal anywhere = conflicting (an error, never resent); failure alone = failure; success only when no failure signal exists anywhere. No exemption applies to a write result: a tenant-shaped answer's LastGraphError is a failure. The body is decoded strictly (cippDecodeStrict): a duplicate object key at any depth, compared case-insensitively, makes the write a failure, because a decoder keeps only one of the two values.
handfixes.why: Codex round 2 on the publish branch: {"Results":["Access denied"]} after a confirmed cipp_execute write came back as a success. For a write a false failure is the safe side: the text is still shown. Adversarial round 2: CIPP's structured success for a password reset ('... will fail if writeback is not enabled ... cannot be turned off', state success) was reported as a failure, and bulk --resume then sent the reset again. Codex round 3: an empty resultText ended the scan and hid "Failed to disable sign-in" in message. Fresh Codex round 1: an explicit success state hid 'The operation failed: access denied'; the write came back as a success and bulk checkpointed it. Fresh Codex round 2: a line opening 'Successfully' hid 'failed to disable sign-in' later in the same text. Fresh Codex round 3: {"state":"success","error":"HTTP 403"} came back as a success and bulk checkpointed it, because "HTTP 403" carries no failure word. Batch 1b Codex round 1: {"Results":["success"],"error":"HTTP 403"} came back as a success because only Results was read; bulk checkpointed it. Batch 1b Codex round 2: {"defaultDomainName":...,"Results":["success"],"LastGraphError":"Failed ..."} and {"Results":["Failed ..."],"Results":["success"]} came back as successes.

handfixes.summary: A bulk --resume checkpoint is keyed by the sha256 of the CSV's bytes and its resolved path, so any edit to the file (whatever its size or modification time) starts a fresh checkpoint.
handfixes.why: The checkpoint was named from the CSV's basename only. Next week's offboards.csv, in any folder, had its first N rows treated as done: bulk sent nothing, printed 0 rows executed and exited 0 (adversarial round 3). Codex round 3: an edit that kept the file's length and modification time reused the checkpoint and skipped the new row.

handfixes.summary: Every successful response body passes the configured-credential funnel. First every character the detector treats as removable (control and Unicode format characters such as U+200B, U+200C, U+200D, U+2060 and U+FEFF, and invalid UTF-8) is stripped from each decoded JSON string and key (or from the text of a non-JSON body). A body up to 1 MiB after normalizing (the most the shared detector scans whole) goes through that detector (exact, escaped, decoded, hex and the rest) over the WHOLE normalized body and the original bytes, with no windowing; if anything is detected, strings, numbers and keys are redacted, serialized and re-checked whole, and any residue withholds the body with a fixed error. A larger body, up to the response size limit (CIPP_MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES), gets a full-length linear scan, with no windowing: the body text and every decoded JSON token (duplicate keys included), with removable characters dropped, as written, with %XX, \xXX and \uXXXX escapes decoded, and with HTML entities decoded, all lowercased, searched for every mask credentialMaskSet builds for each configured credential (exact, URL-escaped, JSON \u-escaped, hex, base64, base32, UTF-16 and the rest) plus standard and URL-safe base64 at all three byte alignments. A hit withholds the whole body with the same fixed error; a body over the response size limit is withheld; otherwise the body comes back byte for byte. Nothing withheld is returned, cached or stored. Then, for every body, whatever would be returned (as it came, or redacted) gets the per-value pass (valuesReveal): every JSON string, key and number, or the whole text of a non-JSON body, has ALL whitespace and every removable character removed FIRST, then the size rule: within recursiveDecodeCap (65536 bytes, where the client's own decoder stops) the full recursive decoding (maskCredentialText: the client decoder and the shared funnel), and any hit withholds the body; over it the body is withheld as too large to check (ErrSuccessBodyValueTooLarge). There is no partial scan, run-splitting or fallback detector for an oversized value. A single value over 64 KiB once spaces are removed, or a non-JSON body over 64 KiB, therefore withholds the response; bodies of any size made of values within the cap pass after full decoding.
handfixes.why: Fresh Codex round 1: only error bodies were funnelled, so a tenant display name repeating the configured bearer reached MCP stdout and the response cache. The shared MCP backstop deliberately skips success results, so the fix sits in this connector's client. Fresh Codex round 2: a JSON number carrying the bearer's hex encoding survived the per-string pass. Fresh Codex round 3: a bearer split by 200000 U+200B characters spanned the 512 KiB detection windows, so the body was returned and cached with the bearer recoverable. Large-body follow-up (ratified in-connector, shared funnel unchanged): withholding every body over 1 MiB refused large tenants' /ListUsers and fanout; the linear scan keeps them while still finding the credential in every encoding, split by zero-width characters, past the 1 MiB mark. Batch 1b Codex round 1: a body past 1 MiB carrying the key base64-encoded twice passed the single-pass linear scan and reached MCP output and the cache. Batch 1b Codex round 2: a text/plain body past 1 MiB carrying the key base64-encoded twice skipped recursive decoding. Final Codex session round 1: one JSON string holding the key base64-encoded twice, cut by spaces and padded with 70000 spaces, passed: spaces kept every base64 run below the shared detector's minimum length, and the client's decoder stops past 64 KiB. Final Codex session round 2: HTML entities split the encoding runs of an oversized value and the full-length scan decoded only the outer layer, so a key written as entities over base64 over base64, padded past the cap, passed. The partial path was removed.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: run success bodies through maskCredentialText in the generated client, not only error bodies.

handfixes.summary: The client resolves auth for every attempt, after rate-limit waits and every Retry-After or backoff sleep, so a token that expired (or will within the refresh skew) is re-minted instead of resent.
handfixes.why: Fresh Codex round 1: auth was resolved once before the retry loop; a token with expires_in 2 and a 429 with Retry-After 3 sent the expired bearer on the retry.

handfixes.summary: A bulk row whose write comes back conflicting (CIPP success state beside failure text) exits non-zero, is never checkpointed as done, and is recorded needs-review with the raw result; no later run (with or without --resume) resends it until the CSV changes. The hold stores only the CSV's sha256, its resolved path's sha256 and row indices (no CIPP response, no row content) in every mode, is saved as soon as the conflict is seen, and bulk --execute refuses to start when this CSV's checkpoint file cannot be opened for writing (or, when it does not exist yet, when the checkpoint folder cannot take a new file).
handfixes.why: Fresh Codex round 1: a conflicting result was either a false success (checkpointed) or, once treated as failure, would be resent by --resume though it may already have taken effect. Fresh Codex round 2: the hold saved CIPP's raw response even under CIPP_NO_LOCAL_DATA=1, and a failed checkpoint write lost the hold. Fresh Codex round 3: an existing read-only checkpoint passed the folder probe, so the hold could not be saved and a re-run resent the write.
